questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: you should read the informations about courses how they work at actual class or you should ask about the courses to students who are in host university when you take the first class in host universitiy. At the same time you should also ask former exchange students about the courses they had and what reccomendations they have.

questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level of the courses variated from course to course, but the general level was very high. At the same time, it was difficult to follow up with some of the courses because of bad study planning and chaos.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the style of teaching was very different from my home university of UCPH. they had more focus of what you could remember than your critical thinking. if the teacher said one thing, then it is how it is.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fundamentos de Lingüística
Usos especializados del Español
Literatura hispanomericana II
Teoría y critíca de la escritura feminina en España
Creación Literaria.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The only specific course I would recommend to future exchange students would be: Creación Literaria. Specific courses I wouldn't recommend would be: Teoría y critíca de la escritura feminina en España and Usos especializados del Español. The level of the courses was too high or had too high expectations for the students, they were even difficult for the spanish students to pass. I would also like to mention that the professor in, Usos especializados del Español, would at times seem scary ort indirectly agressive toward students, and talk down about them, and that would ruin your will for the study. Normally I would have recommended, Literatura hispanomericana II, but there was too many episodes of how badly structured or planned the course was.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say it wasn't that easy to adjust to the local culture, like the siesta, where the lot of the stores are closed. it was also difficult to adjust because everything is closed on sundays.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: no, because in general the students didn't like to interact with erasmus students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The siestas, and sundays where everything is closed.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I would say the food. The tapas was really good.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The three most important things I would say is: 
1. Read the information of the courses. 
2. Ask former exchange students about the courses they had, and their recommendations. 
3. Buy buscard and simcard in Spain, because that's cheaper.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would say you should at least take one course in English, because it can be overwhelming at times. You have to stay strong.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I would say the most rewarding part of my exchange experience was meeting a lot of kind and supporting people from many different places in the world. This can also help with getting more international contacts.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure what to say at this question, because I feel like the whole exchange have been challenging.

questions.answer: Yes
